children: Royal Caribbean
showed it can successfully navigate high fuel costs and still see higher profits thanks to strong booking trends, increased passenger on-board spending, and skill at keeping non-fuel costs down.
Although Royal Caribbean
shifted some

expenses into the fourth quarter, the company increased occupancy by 30 basis points, reduced adjusted cruise costs by 1.8%, and grew revenue by 9%, all of which contributed to a profit of $6.57 per share, up 14% from a year ago.
However, its outlook was mixed: higher EPS guidance was offset by a revenue forecast that fell short of analysts' expectations.

“We suspect RCL is taking a conservative approach to Q4 close-in demand, particularly in the Caribbean, given the additional industry capacity and continued European headwinds,” said Stifel’s Steven Wieczynski, while Jefferies’ David Katz expects 2027 EPS to reflect the favorable impact from the Sandals’ acquisition.
“More important, RCL’s commentary on FY27 is positive, with bookings up high teens and management reiterating FY27 adjusted EPS with a $20 handle,” Katz adds.

“Management noted that since their last earnings call, booking volumes have increased in the mid-teens across all major channels, with 2027 bookings in the high teens, demonstrating strong demand as activity builds in 2027,” said Citi Research analyst James Hardiman, a development that will continue to blunt the impact of fuel volatility and drive RCL closer to the $20/share target.
And it’s not just an increase in the number of bookings but the price passengers are willing to pay, a trend Royal Caribbean CEO Jason Liberty calls “high-quality demand.”

“Our guests are willing to pay more today and tomorrow than they did yesterday,” Liberty said in an interview on CNBC, attributing the phenomenon to the price disparity between cruises and land-based vacations, a value gap that allows RCL to be “insulated from the noise of geopolitics.”
The results coupled with the bullish outlook for the cruise industry is buoying shares of Royal Caribbean
along with rivals Carnival Corp
, Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings
, and Viking Holdings
Norwegian
will report third-quarter results on Thursday, expected to have earned a profit of $0.94 per share on $2.88B in sales, reflecting a gain of 9% in EPS with a 0.6% decline in sales.
Viking Holdings
will report on November 19, expected to have earned a profit of $1.27 per share on $2.21B in sales, a gain of 5.8% and 10%, respectively.

title: Royal Caribbean's strong booking trends, 'high-quality demand,' blunt fuel volatility -- analysts
